topic.title: Asking the Agent a Question
topic.shortdesc: How to use a translation job to ask the agent a question about your content instead of translating, and where to read its answer.

body.p: A translation job does not have to translate. Because the agent reads your project and follows the instructions you give it, you can also use a job to ask a question about your content or translation setup and have the agent report back.

section.title: Asking a Question
section.p: Start a translation job as usual, but in the Instructions field describe your question instead of translation guidance. Tell the agent not to translate anything, and tell it where to put its answer:

ul.li: In a file in your workspace - Ask the agent to write its answer to a file, for example a Markdown report. When the job finishes, bring its results into your workspace and open the file. See Reviewing Translations Before You Commit.
In the execution log - Ask the agent to report its answer in the log. Open it with View log on the job card. See Following and Managing a Translation Job.

section.title: Examples
section.p: Each of these goes in the Instructions field of a new job:

p.codeblock: Do not translate anything. List every topic whose French translation uses a term found in .contentfusion/i18n/forbidden-terms.md, and write the list to report.md.
Do not translate anything. Summarize the structural differences between the en/ and de-DE/ versions of the User Guide publication, and print the summary to the log.

Do not translate anything. Audit this English documentation corpus and identify terms or expressions that lack a suitable dictionary translation into Romanian or whose literal translation would sound unnatural in technical usage. For each term, provide the source term, the recommended translation, and a brief justification. Write one term per line in `terms.txt`.

body.p: Asking a question runs the same agent as a translation job and is subject to the same review discipline: read anything the agent writes into your workspace before you commit it. See Data Handling and Your Responsibilities.
